{{Short description|Soviet scientist (1932–2021)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=August 2021}}
'''Nadir Nadirov''' ({{langx|kk|Нәдір Кәрімұлы Нәдіров}}, ''Nádir Kárimuly Nádirov''; {{langx|ru|Надир Каримович Надиров}}; 6 January 1932 – 24 August 2021<ref>[https://riataza.com/2021/08/24/proshhajte-nadirov-nadir-karimovich/ Прощайте Надиров Надир Каримович!] {{in lang|ru}}</ref>) was a [[Kurds|Kurdish]] engineer<ref>Susan Meislas, ''Kurdistan, In the Shadow of History'', s. 388, Random House, 1997, {{ISBN|0-679-42389-3}}</ref> from [[Kazakhstan]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-08-24|title=Nadir Nadirov yaşamını yitirdi|url=https://gazetekarinca.com/2021/08/nadir-nadirov-yasamini-yitirdi/|access-date=2021-08-26|website=Gazete Karınca|language=tr}}</ref> He was born in the [[Nakhichevan Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic]] and his family was deported to Kazakhstan in 1933.<ref>Susan Meislas, ''Kurdistan, In the Shadow of History'', 388 pp., Random House, 1997, {{ISBN|0-679-42389-3}}</ref> He was the president of association of Kurds in Kazakhstan (''Berbang''<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120713044459/http://eng.gazeta.kz/art.asp?aid=39593|title=GAZETA.KZ ::> Kurdish Diaspora: present and future}}</ref>) and the first vice-president of the Engineering Academy of Kazakhstan. He was also director of the Neft scientific center.<ref>[http://www.jamestown.org/publications_details.php?volume_id=401&issue_id=3094&article_id=2368641 The Jamestown Foundation<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> In 1992, he went public with the accounts of mass deportation of Kurds in the former [[Soviet Union]] during the 1930s and 1940s.<ref>Israel W. Charny, ''The Widening Circle of Genocide'', Transaction Publishers, 1994, {{ISBN|1-56000-172-0}}, p.170</ref>
